To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the trimeric structure of bacteriorodopsin is preserved even after vesicularization and crystal formation; 2) the trimer is arranged in a honeycombed lattice in the crystal; 3) the trimer in the crystal is rotated by 180 degrees with respect to the trimer in purple membrane; and 4) one phospholipid molecule is tightly bound to the trimer and is suggested to be involved in the formation of trimeric structure
the native trimer structure of bacteriorodopsin is preserved even when the in-plane orientation changes, and that one phospholipid molecule acts as a glue in this trimer.

(1) the trimer is a structural unit of bacteriorhodpsin in the purple membrane of H. salinarium, (2) the trimeric units are arranged in a novel honey-comb lattice structure in the planar membrane, (3) the trimer structure is preserved in the lattice, and (4) the phospholipid is tightly bound to the trimeric structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel honeycomb structure of bacteriorhopsin and the role of specific lipid-protein interaction in the structure.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of the structure and function of the bacteriorhodopins.
the elucidation of the structure of the membrane proteins and their interactions with the lipid molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the trimeric bacteriorhodopsins in the honeycomb structure have the same conformation as the trimeric units in the native membrane and are arranged in a novel honeycombed lattice structure, in which a phospholipid molecule acts as a glue.
the lipid-protein interaction is a key factor in the structural stabilization of the membrane protein.
the honeycomb lattice structure is formed by specific lipid-protein interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the honeycomb lattice structure is a new form of lipid-protein interaction, which is different from the hexagonal lattice in purple membrane and the crystalline lattice of the purple membrane crystal.
specific lipid-protein interactions are essential in the assembly process of the purple membrane.
the trimeric bacteriorhodopsins are the building block of the purple membrane and that the phospholipid-protein interactions are essential for the formation of the honeycomb lattice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a lipid-protein interaction in a specific location is essential for the formation of the native structure of the membrane protein.
the trimeric bacteriorhodopsins are the basic building blocks for the assembly of the purple membrane.
a lipid-protein interaction is crucial for maintaining the trimeric structure of bacteriorhopsin in the honeycomb membrane lattice.
